memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Isaac planted crops in that land and the same year reaped a hundredfold, because the LORD blessed him. The man became rich, and his wealth continued to grow until he became very wealthy. He had so many flocks and herds and servants that the Philistines envied him." - Gen 26:12-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Isaac plants in a land still recovering from famine, and reaps a hundredfold. The reason is stated plainly: "because the LORD blessed him." This was God keeping His covenant promise to be with Isaac and prosper him in the land He had given.

We should be careful how we read this. It does not mean that faith always leads to wealth, or that riches are proof of God's favour. Isaac's abundance was part of a specific covenant promise, and even here, his growing wealth soon brought trouble — the Philistines envied him. Prosperity is not a simple reward system; God's deepest blessing was His presence, not merely his cattle.

Still, there is a lasting truth: everything good in our lives ultimately comes from God's hand (Jas 1:17). Whatever harvest we enjoy — a home, work, health, relationships — is His gift, not merely the fruit of our own cleverness. A grateful heart traces every good thing back to the Giver.

Notice also the shadow side: success can attract envy. When God blesses us, not everyone celebrates. That is not a reason to hide His goodness, but a call to stay humble and gracious. Receive what God gives with thankfulness, hold it with open hands, and let your blessings become a means of blessing others.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I trace the good in my life back to God as the Giver?
2. Am I holding what God has given with humility and open hands?
3. How do I respond when someone else is blessed — with joy or envy?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, every good thing I have comes from You. Keep me humble and grateful, and let me use Your blessings to bless others rather than to boast. Amen.
